title: The Trouble with Geniuses, Part 1
coreMove: The threshold effect means intelligence is crucial up to a point, but beyond that point success depends on other traits, supports, and opportunities.

exampleSpecs.stakes: tiny score gaps may hide better evidence of fit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Chris Langan to challenge a score-heavy hiring decision.

exampleSpecs.stakes: a child may be judged by one early score for years
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use Terman's Termites to audit high-IQ selection.

exampleSpecs.stakes: teams may keep ranking a trait after it has served its purpose
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the basketball height analogy to rank recruits.

exampleSpecs.stakes: marginal score differences may decide life-changing support
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Apply threshold reasoning to scholarship awards.

exampleSpecs.stakes: students may be trained to chase rank instead of harder growth
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the Termites to review gifted-team sorting.

exampleSpecs.stakes: a gifted researcher may stall without conditions for output
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the threshold effect to mentor a brilliant researcher.
